description: WifiHaven Plain support integration (#2199 + #2200, epic #2197): server-signed widget-identity outcomes, household→Plain customer-upsert outcomes, the #2200 Claude responder's webhook outcomes (support_ai_draft_total{outcome,reason} from SupportResponder — dispatched / email_registered_dispatched / email_unregistered_rejected / email_reject_send_failed / skipped_unauthenticated / origin_lookup_failed / skipped_not_inbound / rate_limited / invalid_signature / malformed / disabled / error), and the cloud agent's callback actions (support_agent_action_total{op,outcome} — reply / issue / household_read). All labels are bounded enums (never per-email / per-household / per-thread). The responder runs iff the explicit support.responderEnabled flag is set (#2265 — no dark-by-default; a true flag with missing config refuses to boot); disabled installs count outcomes as disabled and dispatch nothing — as does a LIVE responder whose Plain write half is off (plain.writeEnabled=false), which decides a static reject and never sends it (#2471), so outcome=disabled does not by itself mean the responder is dark. See issues #2206, #2200, #2241, #2265. #2419 adds the data-access consent lifecycle (support_consent_total{outcome} — the agent's REQUEST vs the customer's grant/revoke, plus the household-mismatch guard): consent is recorded server-side from the customer's own authenticated action, so the agent can ask but can never self-grant. #2438 adds support_dispatch_total{outcome,transport} — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome (dispatched / error / disabled) at the transport boundary, isolating a silent non-2xx trigger failure the conflated draft metric can't surface. #2505 makes the email-intake gate a second producer of support_customer_upsert_total, so a customer who only ever emails support is mapped onto their household instead of keeping a null externalId forever. #2435 adds the `reason` label to support_customer_upsert_total (panel 18): the household→Plain customer mapping can be permanently blocked by Plain's workspace-wide customer-email uniqueness, so `reason` separates a self-healed collision (reconciled) from a BROKEN, non-self-healing mapping (email_collision / permission / schema / tenant_missing) and from a transient miss (error). #2437 adds operator_escalation_total{channel="support",kind,outcome} — the operator-notification funnel behind an escalation — plus the support_agent_action_total ops escalate (the agent's structural handoff) and escalate_mark (the SERVER's Plain addLabels write that makes the handoff visible in the inbox). #2453 makes the consent link single-use (a nonce consumed on redemption, V85) and strips it out of every route into the agent's own kickoff, adding the link_spent / link_stale refusal outcomes; #2454 refuses public-issue filing from a session holding the consented-read scope (support_consent_total{outcome="issue_refused_data_session"}, and support_agent_action_total{op="issue",outcome="denied_data_session"}). #2477 adds the dispatch WATCHDOG pair — agent_dispatch_unreplied{channel="support"} (a gauge of the customers waiting RIGHT NOW on a session that accepted the trigger and never called back) and agent_dispatch_sweeps_total{channel="support"} (the sweep's own heartbeat). Both are written on EVERY DispatchTracker.sweep tick including the healthy one, so "nobody is waiting" is a visible explicit zero rather than an absence indistinguishable from a detector that never ran (#2546). Alerts W11 (a dispatch died past the agent-token TTL — that customer got nothing) and W12 (the watchdog stopped reporting) are grounded on them. Support only: press dispatch is not paired with its callback until #2517, so no press-channel sweep exists and NOTHING alerts on a missing press watchdog today; the press dashboard's panels land with that issue.

panels.title: Widget identity requests (cumulative, issued)
panels.description: sum(support_widget_identity_total{outcome="issued"}) — total server-signed identities issued to authenticated admins. Zero while the widget is dark (no Plain app id / identity secret).

panels.title: Widget identity rate by outcome
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_widget_identity_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — issued / no_email (caller has no email to identify — username-only admin) / disabled (Plain widget unconfigured, feature dark). A rising no_email share means admins without an email are opening the app; disabled dominates until the operator provisions the Plain widget keys.

panels.title: Household → Plain customer upsert outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_customer_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — ok (mapping written to Plain, whether first-try or reconciled) / disabled (Plain write API explicitly off, #2266) / error (Plain returned non-2xx or a GraphQL error; fail-open, the identity response is unaffected). A persistent 'error' share means the household→customer mapping isn't reaching Plain. Two producers write this series (#2505): the SPA identity path and the email-intake gate. This panel is the aggregate; the '#2435' panel splits it by reason so a BROKEN, non-self-healing mapping (email_collision / permission / schema / tenant_missing) is distinguishable from a transient miss.

panels.title: Responder webhook outcomes (#2200)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — dispatched (a cloud-agent session was created for a UI-originated thread) / email_registered_dispatched (#2307: a NEW inbound email whose From matched a registered household admin, admitted to the AI bound to that household) / email_unregistered_rejected (#2307: a NEW inbound email from an unregistered address got the FIXED static reject — NO Claude call, NO tokens burned) / email_reject_send_failed (#2471: that reject was DECIDED but Plain REFUSED the send, so the customer got nothing — expect a flat zero; a sustained rate means the Plain workspace cannot send at all) / skipped_unauthenticated (a continuation with no resolvable tenant) / origin_lookup_failed (#2462: resolving the origin THREW — a households/users read failed — so we never established whether the sender is registered; the delivery is dropped rather than rejected as unregistered. Expect a flat zero; also logs at ERROR naming the stage) / skipped_not_inbound (#2403 loop guard: our own outbound thread.chat_sent reply, a non-customer actor, or a bodyless metadata event — never dispatched) / rate_limited (the per-thread + global dispatch, or the global reject, cost caps fired) / invalid_signature (unsigned or forged webhook — security-relevant, investigate a sustained rate) / malformed / disabled (an EXPLICIT named flag is off, so nothing was attempted — either responderEnabled=false, the whole responder dark, OR plain.writeEnabled=false, a LIVE responder whose Plain write half is dark, in which case a static reject is decided and never sent; #2471) / error (Managed Agents dispatch failed). Emitted by SupportResponder.handleWebhook.

panels.title: Agent callback actions (#2200/#2241)
panels.description: sum by (op, outcome) (rate(support_agent_action_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatched cloud agent's token-authenticated callbacks: reply (post the AI-attributed reply into the token-bound Plain thread — sent to the customer, autonomous send), issue (file a PII-scrubbed, support-agent-labeled GitHub issue), household_read (the consented single-household summary), consent_request (#2419, the server's fixed data-access prompt), escalate (#2437, the agent handing off to a human) and escalate_mark (the SERVER's Plain addLabels write that makes the handoff visible in the inbox). outcome=denied covers bad/expired tokens AND consent-less household reads; outcome=error on op=household_read (#2462) means the consented account read did not COMPLETE — a repo query threw, so the read was refused (5xx) rather than answered with a synthesized empty summary; rate_limited is the per-thread/global issue caps; ok_no_link (#2461) is a SUCCESSFUL issue filing whose link we could not read back from GitHub's response — count it WITH ok for filing volume, and if it is the only success value rising, the target repo was likely renamed or transferred (the log line names that cause). Emitted by SupportResponder.

panels.title: Agent-filed issues (24h) — volume alert feed
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="issue",outcome=~"ok|ok_no_link|ok_duplicate"}[24h])) — issue-filing ASKS the support agent completed in the last 24h (the #2241 volume-alert feed). The per-thread (3/h) + global (10/h) rate limits cap the ceiling; a value near the cap means the agent is filing aggressively — review the support-agent label on GitHub. Counts EVERY success outcome: `ok_no_link` (#2461) is a real filed issue whose link we could not read back, and `ok_duplicate` (#2458) is an ask absorbed by the search-before-file check — an already-open issue covered the topic, so nothing new was created. Excluding either would under-report what the agent is doing; note that with `ok_duplicate` included this is the ASK rate, so it is no longer identical to the count of issues actually created. For the created count over this same 24h window, subtract the deduped asks: sum(increase(support_issue_dedup_total{env="$env",outcome="matched"}[24h])) — `IssueOutcome.Duplicate` is the sole producer of both `ok_duplicate` and `matched`, so they are emitted 1:1. (The duplicate-check timeseries panel is a 5m rate, so do not read the subtraction off it directly.)

panels.title: Agent sessions dispatched (24h) — cost watch
panels.description: sum(increase(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="dispatched"}[24h])) — cloud-agent sessions started in the last 24h. Each session bills API tokens (rough order: $0.10–$0.50/draft on Sonnet 5); the global dispatch cap (50/day) bounds the ceiling. Red at the cap = sustained widget spam or a webhook retry loop — check the rate_limited outcome on the webhook panel.

panels.title: Household → Plain tenant entitlement upsert outcomes (#2240)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_tenant_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the household→Plain TENANT write (household name + plan/founding tenant fields), separate from the customer upsert. ok (name + all fields written) / error (tenant upsert failed, or a field write failed). Fail-open, the identity response is unaffected. This panel is the aggregate; the '#2410' panel next to it slices error by reason so a PROVISIONING GAP (permission / schema — needs a fix) is distinguishable from a transient tenant/field hiccup.

panels.title: Entitlement write failures by reason — provisioning-gap watch (#2410)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_tenant_upsert_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the household→Plain entitlement write failed. permission (the machine-user API key lacks the tenantField:* permission — grant it, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1) and schema (the plan/founding tenant-field schemas are not registered in the Plain workspace — register them, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §7.3) are PROVISIONING GAPS: they will NEVER self-heal until fixed, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix inline. tenant / field_write are the transient/other bucket (a Plain hiccup — usually self-heals). ALERT on any sustained permission or schema rate; a transient tenant/field_write blip is expected noise.

panels.title: Data-access consent lifecycle (#2419)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_consent_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the in-conversation data-access consent flow. AGENT side: requested (the agent asked, so the SERVER posted its consent prompt into the thread), request_already_granted, request_rate_limited (per-thread cap), request_disabled / request_error (the Plain write). CUSTOMER side, on POST /api/support/consent: granted, revoked (withdrawn ahead of expiry), revoke_noop (a withdrawal of a grant that was not live — idempotent for the customer, but not a real withdrawal), invalid / expired (a bad or stale consent link), household_mismatch. Bounded enum — never a per-household / per-thread label. Emitted by SupportResponder. Healthy flow: `requested` followed by `granted`; sustained `requested` with no `granted` means customers are not completing the link (check the SPA /support/consent page and that they are signed in). #2476 adds two AGENT-side read outcomes: read_no_scope (a token minted without data scope — the common case) and read_withdrawn (a token that WAS minted with data scope, presented after the customer withdrew: the household read re-reads the grant on every call, so a withdrawal bites on the very next read rather than at token expiry). A rising read_withdrawn means grants are being pulled mid-conversation. #2453/#2454 add three refusal outcomes, all of which write nothing and should read flat zero: link_spent (a single-use consent link re-presented after its grant was withdrawn or lapsed — the replay shape), link_stale (a link minted BEFORE the withdrawal it would otherwise undo), and issue_refused_data_session (a consented-read session refused public-issue filing, because household and profile names are ordinary words no scrubber can catch).

panels.title: Consent links redeemed by the WRONG household (24h) — expect 0
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome="household_mismatch"}[24h])) — a consent link minted for household A presented by a household-B session. Nothing is written when this fires (the grant endpoint refuses it), but a NON-ZERO value means links are being shared or replayed across tenants and deserves a look at the threads involved (#2419 security boundary).

panels.title: Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes (#2438)
panels.description: sum by (outcome, transport) (rate(support_dispatch_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome, measured at the transport boundary (CloudAgentObservability): dispatched (the Managed Agents session / Claude Code Cloud routine trigger returned 2xx) / error (the trigger returned non-2xx or the call threw — the cloud agent NEVER started) / disabled (the responder is dark, #2265; carries no transport). transport ∈ managed-agents (API-credit billed) | claude-code-cloud (subscription billed). This is the series the #2408 go-live gap needed: the webhook panel's 'dispatched' outcome only means a session was ATTEMPTED — a silent non-2xx trigger failure shows up as 'error' HERE and nowhere else. ALERT on any sustained 'error' rate while the responder is enabled (each is a support reply that never went out). Emitted for BOTH audiences from one shared envelope; the press twin is press_dispatch_total on the Press dashboard. #2416: when outcome=error, the 'Support dispatch failures by reason' panel below splits that bucket into config (a permanent 4xx misconfiguration — a dead responder needing a human fix, alert W6) vs transient (a 5xx/transport blip). #2472: this series ALSO carries the COMPLETION half of the pair — completed (a terminal agent callback arrived for a dispatch we recorded), callback_slow (nothing after 10 min; a usage-limit-suspended claude-code-cloud run legitimately reaches this, so an occasional sample is normal), no_callback (nothing by the agent-token TTL — the session accepted the trigger and DIED, and the customer got no answer). Read 'dispatched' against 'completed': before #2472 a dispatched-then-dead session counted only as a success.

panels.title: Thread-history reads — responder context watch (#2430)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_thread_history_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the per-dispatch Plain thread-timeline read that gives the STATELESS support responder its conversation context (a fresh cloud session fires per inbound message, so without this read the agent answers every follow-up in isolation). PROVISIONING / DRIFT buckets, none of which self-heal — alert on any sustained rate: permission (the Plain machine-user API key lacks thread:read — grant it, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1), schema (Plain rejected the query — a timeline-schema drift), unparsed (Plain returned turn-SHAPED entries — chat/email, not notes or status flips — and NONE parsed into a turn: the actor/entry union shapes drifted). Each of those is also logged at ERROR with the fix inline. NORMAL buckets: ok (the read returned at least one turn — note this measures the READ, not how much CONTEXT the agent got: Plain fires the webhook once the inbound message is already on the timeline, so even a genuine first message normally reads back its own echo, which the API then strips), empty (Plain returned no readable timeline entries at all — rare, NOT the common first-message case), error (a transient miss or timeout — occasional is noise), disabled (the Plain client is unconfigured). The read is FAIL-OPEN — every non-ok outcome degrades to "dispatch with the latest message alone" — so this panel is the only way a permanently context-less responder is visible.

panels.title: Support dispatch failures by reason — dead-responder watch (#2416)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the support cloud agent could not be dispatched. Complements the #2438 'Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes' panel, which counts dispatch attempts by {outcome,transport}: this one splits the ERROR bucket by cause. config = a non-self-healing 4xx at the Anthropic boundary: a revoked/wrong anthropicApiKey (401), a wrong claudeAgentId / claudeEnvironmentId / claudeCodeRoutineId (404), or a STALE hard-coded anthropic-beta header (400). Those NEVER self-heal — the responder is dead until a human rotates the key, fixes the id, or bumps the header, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix named inline. transient = transport / timeout / 5xx, plus the 4xx that ARE load/timing signals (408, 429) — expected noise. ALERT on any sustained 'config' rate (warning rule W6, infra/grafana/alerting-rules-warning.tf); ignore isolated 'transient' blips. Dispatch is fail-open by design, so the webhook keeps returning 200 either way.

panels.title: Escalations to a human (#2437)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="support",kind="escalated"}[5m])) — #2437. Every support thread the AI handed off, by how the operator notice landed. A rising rate means the responder is escalating more than expected. Any series that is not `sent` means a human was owed a notice and did not get the email (failed = Resend rejected it, skipped_disabled = the email transport is off, skipped_no_recipient = no wifihaven.email.operatorAddress); the in-Plain needs-human label is the second, independent channel (see the unmarked-threads panel).

panels.title: Escalated threads NOT marked in Plain (24h) — expect 0 (#2437)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="escalate_mark",outcome=~"error|disabled"}[24h])) — the server's Plain addLabels write failed, so an escalated thread is INVISIBLE under the needs-a-human inbox filter and the operator is back to reading every thread. Non-zero is a provisioning gap, not a blip: check wifihaven.support.plain.escalationLabelTypeId and that the Plain machine-user API key carries the `label:create` permission (docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1).

panels.title: Support escalations handed off (24h) (#2437)
panels.description: sum(increase(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="support",kind="escalated"}[24h])) — how many support conversations the AI handed to a human in the last 24h. Not an error signal: it is the human-workload number, and the counterweight to support_ai_draft_total when asking whether the assistant is resolving enough on its own.

panels.title: Customer↔household mapping by reason — broken-mapping watch (#2435)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_customer_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — HOW the household→Plain customer mapping resolved. ok = upserted on the first try (the common path). reconciled = the household admin's email was already held by a Plain customer with NO externalId (Plain auto-creates one from an inbound support email, #2198), and we bound it onto the household by patching externalId + joining the tenant — a self-healed collision, expected on any household that emailed support before loading the widget. #2505 widens WHO produces this series: the upsert now also runs from the EMAIL-INTAKE gate (SupportResponder) the moment an inbound From resolves to a registered household admin, not just from the SPA identity path — so a customer who only ever emails is mapped too. Same series, same reason vocabulary, so a broken mapping is attributable here regardless of which producer attempted it; expect the `reconciled` share to grow once the email producer is live, since Plain auto-creates that customer from the inbound email before we ever write it — the series has no producer label (bounded-label rule), so the two producers are not separable on this panel — `reason` is the axis that matters here anyway. email_collision = that reconcile FAILED for no more specific cause: the mapping is BROKEN and will NEVER self-heal (the email is taken forever), so the household's widget messages resolve no tenantIdentifier and fall through to the email-intake fallback or are dropped as skipped_unauthenticated. permission (the machine-user lacks customer:edit for the upsert, or customerTenantMembership:create for the household-membership join — a reconcile leg attributes these too, not just the primary upsert) and schema (our UpsertCustomerInput no longer matches Plain's schema) are the other non-self-healing PROVISIONING GAPS. ALERT on any sustained email_collision / permission / schema / tenant_missing rate — each is a fix, not a blip, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix named inline. tenant_missing = the membership join had no TENANT to join to because the tenant write itself FAILED; do NOT debug it from this panel — the specific cause is on support_tenant_upsert_total{reason=tenant} (panel 9, 'Entitlement write failures by reason'), and this join cannot succeed until that write does. error = the transient/other bucket (including a join whose tenant was merely SKIPPED for want of household context — a degraded repo read the next identity call repairs); disabled = the write API is explicitly off (#2266).

panels.title: Agent callbacks REFUSED at the token check (#2473)
panels.description: sum by (op, reason) (rate(agent_token_rejected_total{env="$env",channel="support"}[5m])) — Every sample is a cloud-agent callback we REFUSED at the token check — an answer that was generated and then thrown away at the door, so the customer/journalist received nothing. token_expired = a token WE minted outlived its TTL: the #2473 failure, where a claude-code-cloud run paused on subscription usage limits and resumed after the token had died. Sustained non-zero token_expired means agentTokenTtlMinutes is again shorter than the transport's real round-trip latency — raise it (api/src/Config.scala, AgentTokenTtl). invalid = malformed or wrongly-signed (a probe, or a secret rotation mid-flight); missing = no bearer at all. Both agent endpoints are public, so a low invalid/missing background rate is internet noise; token_expired never is.

panels.title: Support answers lost to an EXPIRED token (24h) — expect 0 (#2473)
panels.description: sum(increase(agent_token_rejected_total{env="$env",channel="support",reason="token_expired"}[24h])) — each one is a customer who asked a question, had it answered by the agent, and received nothing. Non-zero means the agent-token TTL is shorter than how long a paused cloud-agent run takes to resume; the API also logs each at ERROR. This is the exact #2473 failure, made visible.

panels.title: Consent grants that dead-ended (24h) — expect 0
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome=~"resume_rate_limited|resume_disabled|resume_error|resume_config_error"}[24h])) — #2460: a customer granted data access and the server FAILED to close the loop for them. Every grant emits exactly one resume_* outcome. Benign ones: resumed (the customer's last question was re-dispatched under the new scope — the happy path), resume_no_message (no CUSTOMER turn was readable on the thread — an empty or failed timeline read, or a recent history carrying none — so the fixed server-authored nudge posted instead; check the thread-history panel for a thread:read/timeline:read gap), resume_skipped (a re-confirmed LIVE grant — the idempotency guard doing its job). The four counted HERE are the ones where the customer gets nothing back: resume_rate_limited (the thread hit its dispatch cap — the grant landed, the follow-up did not), resume_disabled (the dispatcher or Plain client is unconfigured), resume_error (a transient dispatch/write failure), and resume_config_error (a permanent 4xx at the agent boundary — the #2416 split; cross-check the dispatch-failures-by-reason panel). Sustained non-zero means customers are granting permission and still being left waiting — the exact symptom #2460 fixed.

panels.title: Plain API-key permission gaps at boot (24h) — expect 0 (#2452)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_permission_probe_total{env="$env",outcome=~"missing|broken"}[24h])) — the BOOT-time audit of the Plain machine-user API key's OWN permission array (Plain's `myPermissions` query) found a PERMANENT problem: `missing` = a required permission is not granted; `broken` = Plain rejected the request with a 4xx (a revoked, rotated, or wrong key; a wrong endpoint) or its probe shape drifted, meaning EVERY Plain call is failing, not just the probe. Neither is fixable by a redeploy: the permission array is Plain-WORKSPACE state, set only via the `updateApiKey` mutation. Every Plain call gated on a missing permission 403s, and because those paths are fail-open the feature behind them is simply INERT — thread history (#2430) means the responder answers every follow-up with no memory; tenant fields (#2240) mean the operator sees no entitlement. The boot ERROR log names EVERY missing permission at once plus the exact mutation to paste. Expect 0; non-zero is actionable immediately (docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1). Note `unreachable` is deliberately NOT counted here — that means Plain did not answer, so the grants are merely unverified this boot.

panels.title: Plain API-key permission audit by outcome (#2452)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (increase(support_permission_probe_total{env="$env"}[$__rate_interval])) — one sample per API boot (#2452). ok = every permission this deployment's enabled features need is granted. missing = required permissions absent. broken = Plain returned a 4xx (rejected credential, wrong endpoint) or its probe shape drifted. missing and broken are both PERMANENT provisioning gaps, both logged at ERROR, and both counted on the stat panel beside this one — neither self-heals. unreachable = transport / timeout / 5xx / the self-healing 408 + 429, i.e. we could not ask; it says NOTHING about what is granted and is expected to be transient, which is exactly why it is a separate bucket — folding a rejected credential into it would tell an operator to wait out a problem that never resolves (the #2416 config-vs-transient boundary). skipped = the Plain write client is unconfigured (the self-hosted posture), nothing to audit.

panels.title: Static rejects Plain REFUSED to send (24h) — expect 0 (#2471)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="email_reject_send_failed"}[24h])) — an unregistered-sender reject was decided correctly and Plain refused to DELIVER it, so the customer got nothing. Non-zero is a PROVISIONING GAP, not a blip: the usual cause is the Plain workspace having email sending switched off — Settings → Channels → Email §3 "Sending emails" left unverified, or §4 "Enable email" never clicked (docs/ops/plain-setup.md §3.1). Grep the API log for `plain replyToThread failed` for the message Plain returned. This series exists because the reject used to meter as email_unregistered_rejected even when the send failed (#2471, found on staging 2026-07-26), so the outcomes panel read healthy while ZERO rejects were delivered. An explicitly-disabled write half (wifihaven.support.plain.writeEnabled=false) does NOT appear here — that meters as outcome=disabled.

panels.title: Dispatched sessions that NEVER called back (24h) — expect 0 (#2472)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_dispatch_total{env="$env",outcome="no_callback"}[24h])) — a cloud-agent session that ACCEPTED the trigger and then died: no /api/support/agent/reply, /escalate, or /request-consent call ever arrived within the agent-token TTL (DispatchTracker.deadAfterFor = support.agentTokenTtlMinutes, 24h by default). The TTL is the threshold because it is the first instant at which silence is unambiguous: BEFORE it a claude-code-cloud run suspended on subscription usage limits can still resume and answer — possibly the next morning (#2473 / AgentTokenTtl) — and AFTER it that resumed run's callback 401s, so the answer can never reach the customer. Every sample is a customer who wrote to support and got NOTHING back. Observed live on staging 2026-07-26 (#2335 validation, test #6a): the dispatch half logged and metered a clean success, the reply half simply never happened — total to the customer, invisible to us. NOTHING RETRIES: auto-retry was deliberately declined (a second billed session plus a duplicate-reply risk the #2403 loop guard cannot suppress), so a non-zero value is an ACTION for a human — read the thread in Plain and reply by hand. That is safe at THIS threshold and only at this threshold: a late agent reply can no longer land, so hand-replying cannot produce a duplicate. Correlate with the API log line `support dispatch NEVER CALLED BACK`, which names the thread, household, and transport.

panels.title: Dispatches still unanswered after 10 min (24h) (#2472)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_dispatch_total{env="$env",outcome="callback_slow"}[24h])) — a dispatch with no terminal agent callback after DispatchTracker.SlowAfter (10 min), against healthy replies observed landing in 30–110s. This is the WARN tier, NOT an error: a claude-code-cloud routine run can be suspended on subscription usage limits and resumed hours later (#2473 / AgentTokenTtl), and those runs do answer, sometimes the next morning — so occasional samples are expected, each dispatch is counted here at most once, and a thread on this panel must NOT be hand-replied blind (wait for the no_callback panel, which is past the point a late reply can land). What matters is the SHAPE: a sustained rate, or one that tracks the no_callback panel, means sessions are stalling rather than pausing. Log line: `support dispatch still unanswered`.

panels.title: Issue-filing duplicate check (#2458)
panels.description: sum by (outcome, reason) (rate(support_issue_dedup_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the search-before-file check that runs on EVERY support-agent issue filing. outcome: matched = an already-open `support-agent` issue covered the topic, so nothing was created and the customer was pointed at that issue instead (the fix working, not a fault); no_match = we looked and filed; scan_error = we could NOT look and filed WITHOUT checking. reason attributes a scan_error: permission (401/403/404 — the bot token cannot LIST issues on wifihaven/wifihaven) and schema (a 2xx body we could not decode — GitHub's list shape drifted) NEVER self-heal and are each logged at ERROR with the fix named; transient (transport, timeout, 5xx) may; none rides every non-error sample. The dedup is deliberately fail-open — a scan failure must never block a genuine report — which is exactly why the reason split matters: a permanently blind check still files successfully and reads healthy everywhere else, and its only other symptom is duplicate issues quietly reappearing (the #2458 defect). The expect-0 stat beside this counts permission+schema only.

panels.title: Duplicate check PERMANENTLY blind (24h) — expect 0 (#2458)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_issue_dedup_total{env="$env",outcome="scan_error",reason=~"permission|schema"}[24h])) — issues filed WITHOUT a duplicate check for a reason that NEVER self-heals: `permission` = the fine-grained bot token cannot LIST issues on wifihaven/wifihaven (grant it Issues:read), `schema` = GitHub's list-issues response shape drifted past GithubIssueClient.ListedIssue. Because the dedup is fail-open, the filing still succeeds and the volume panel beside it still reads healthy, so this is the ONLY place a permanently-blind check is visible — the other symptom is duplicate issues quietly returning. Deliberately EXCLUDES reason=transient (timeouts, 5xx), which is expected to be non-zero and self-healing; folding it in would make this panel cry wolf and stop being read. Both counted reasons are also logged at ERROR with the fix named — grep the API log for `github duplicate scan`.

panels.title: Live routine prompt version (#2469)
panels.description: sum by (state) (rate(agent_prompt_version_total{env="$env",channel="support"}[5m])) — what the LIVE cloud agent reports as its OWN prompt version on each reply callback, compared against the version compiled from deploy/support-agent/agent.yaml. current = the running agent matches this build. stale = it is answering customers from an OLDER prompt: the Claude Code Cloud routine prompt is web-UI-only, so a merged prompt change stays inert until an operator re-pastes it at claude.ai/code/routines — and until they do, the routine reports a GREEN run while behaving from the old prompt (#2419/#2425 consent and #2430/#2441 thread history both shipped that way). unknown = the agent reported no version at all, most likely a routine still on a pre-#2469 prompt. Alert-only: a mismatch never fails a webhook or drops a reply.

panels.title: Support replies from a DRIFTED routine (24h) — expect 0 (#2469)
panels.description: sum(increase(agent_prompt_version_total{env="$env",channel="support",state=~"stale|unknown"}[24h])) — each one is a customer answered by a routine whose prompt does not match this build. This is the #2469 failure made visible: a stale routine told customers "reply here confirming you're OK with me accessing your account", which grants nothing, while every run reported green. The fix is manual and takes a minute: re-paste the system: block from deploy/support-agent/agent.yaml into the support routine at claude.ai/code/routines, preserving the <routine-fire-payload> opt-in (deploy/support-agent/README.md, 'post-merge re-paste'). Expect a burst right after any PR that changed that prompt merges — that is the detector working, not a bug.

panels.title: Consent links REPLAYED after withdrawal (24h) — expect 0 (#2453)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome=~"link_spent|link_stale"}[24h])) — #2453: a well-signed, unexpired consent link presented when it cannot legitimately grant. `link_spent` is a SINGLE-USE link re-presented once its grant was withdrawn or lapsed — the replay shape, and the security-interesting one: the consent prompt is posted through the machine-user write path, so since #2430/#2441 the live link re-enters the agent's own prompt as thread history and could be captured there. `link_stale` is a link minted BEFORE the customer's withdrawal, which must not silently undo it. Neither writes a grant, so a non-zero value is an attempt, not a breach — but it means links are being re-presented and deserves a look at the threads involved. A customer double-clicking Allow does NOT land here, sequentially or concurrently: while the grant is still live a re-presented link is an idempotent no-op counted as `granted` (the repo re-reads liveness after the nonce INSERT serializes, so the loser of a concurrent first redemption still sees the committed grant).

panels.title: Issue filing refused in a data-access session (24h) — expect 0 (#2454)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome="issue_refused_data_session"}[24h])) — #2454: an agent session whose token carries the consented-read scope tried to file a PUBLIC GitHub issue. The two capabilities are refused as a pair, structurally, because the consented read returns the household name and the profile names (by product design, typically children's given names) — ordinary words that match no SupportPrivacy.scrubForIssue pattern and never will. Nothing is published when this fires, and the refusal happens before the rate limiters and before the #2458 duplicate scan. Expect a flat zero: the kickoff prompt tells the agent the endpoint will refuse this token, so a non-zero rate means the prompt and the enforcement disagree — or that something is trying. Cross-check support_agent_action_total{op="issue",outcome="denied_data_session"} on the agent-callback panel.

panels.title: Agent CREDENTIAL redactions (24h) — expect 0 (#2508)
panels.description: sum by (op, reason) (increase(agent_reply_redacted_total{env="$env",channel="support"}[24h])) — each sample is a support agent that put a credential into text we were about to send — a customer-visible Plain reply, an operator escalation note, or a PUBLIC GitHub issue. The AgentCredential redactor removed it before send, so nothing leaked; the sample means the agent TRIED. reason=agent_token is the severe case — it quoted a session token this system minted, which is what a successful prompt-injection exfiltration looks like. reason=bearer is any other credential-shaped Bearer value pasted out of its environment. Each is also logged at ERROR (the log never quotes the credential). Non-zero warrants reading the thread in Plain.

panels.title: Consented household reads that FAILED (24h) — expect 0 (#2462)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="household_read",outcome="error"}[24h])) — the agent asked for the customer's account summary and a repo query THREW, so the read was refused (5xx) and the agent was told it has no data. Non-zero means customers asking account questions in that window were told we couldn't reach their account details instead of getting an answer — check Postgres health and grep the API log for `agent household read FAILED`, which carries the household, the thread, and the driver message. This series exists because the four reads used to be individually swallowed into an EMPTY summary metered ok (#2462): a total DB outage and a brand-new household produced the identical "0 devices, 0 profiles" answer, which the agent stated to the customer as account fact and then built troubleshooting advice on top of. A household that GENUINELY has nothing is NOT counted here — it still meters ok with real zeros. The distinction is failure-vs-empty, not zero-vs-nonzero.

panels.title: Webhook origins we could NOT look up (24h) — expect 0 (#2462)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="origin_lookup_failed"}[24h])) — resolving an inbound delivery's origin (the UI-origin households read, or the #2307 admin-email users read) THREW, so we never established whether the sender is a registered customer. The delivery is dropped: nothing dispatched, nothing said to the customer. Non-zero means real customer messages went unanswered — check Postgres health and grep the API log for `origin lookup FAILED`, which names the failing stage (tenant_household | admin_email | admin_household). This outcome is deliberately NOT folded into skipped_unauthenticated or email_unregistered_rejected: both of those ASSERT the sender has no registered origin, and acting on that assertion during a DB blip is what sent a registered, paying admin the #2307 "you're not a registered customer" static reject — metered as a routine reject, so nothing recorded it was wrong.

panels.title: CONSENT THEATRE: grants with no read behind them (24h) — expect <= 0 (#2665)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome="granted"}[24h])) - sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="household_read",outcome="ok"}[24h])) — data-access grants in the window MINUS successful consented reads in the same window. This is the #2665 signal: a customer made a security decision, a 24h grant went live, and the agent then read nothing against it — the grant bought them nothing, and the session was ALSO degraded for its whole life (a dataAccess=true session is structurally refused issue filing, #2454). That is exactly what happened on the first real prod support conversation: the customer asked for today's screen time, granted access, and the agent could not answer because HouseholdSummary carried no usage at all. Reading it: > 0 means grants are outrunning reads — either the agent is requesting consent for questions the read cannot answer (widen the payload, or teach it not to ask), or it is granted and then never calls the endpoint. <= 0 is healthy: a granted session legitimately reads more than once. This is a COARSE difference of two independent counters, not a per-grant join — a grant late in the window whose read lands after it shows transiently, so read the trend, not one sample.

panels.title: Consented household reads that SUCCEEDED (24h) — the grant being USED (#2665)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="household_read",outcome="ok"}[24h])) — consented account reads that SUCCEEDED. Its absence is the thing to notice: before #2665 this series did not exist in prod at all, and "the agent never read" was indistinguishable from "the metric is mis-wired". Since #2665 the read carries today's per-profile screen time (used / limit / remaining / blocked-right-now) plus the device→profile map, so a granted session answering a usage question WILL land here. Zero over a window in which support_consent_total{outcome="granted"} is non-zero is the consent-theatre panel's input.

panels.title: Customers waiting on an unanswered dispatch — a WRITTEN zero (#2477)
panels.description: agent_dispatch_unreplied{env="$env",channel="support"} — #2477, the dispatch WATCHDOG. How many customers are waiting RIGHT NOW on a cloud-agent session that accepted the trigger and has not come back, past DispatchTracker.SlowAfter (10 min, sized in #2472 against healthy replies observed landing in 30–110s). Read it as a LEVEL, not a rate: a dispatch enters this count 10 minutes after it fires and leaves it either when the agent calls back or when it is declared dead at the agent-token TTL (DispatchTracker.deadAfterFor = support.agentTokenTtlMinutes, 24h by default via AgentTokenTtl.DefaultMinutes), at which point it is counted once on support_dispatch_total{outcome="no_callback"} instead. WHY THIS PANEL EXISTS ALONGSIDE THOSE COUNTERS: they only move when something is wrong, so a healthy system emitted NOTHING and "nobody is waiting", "the responder was never enabled" and "the sweep fiber died" were one indistinguishable picture — the #2546 failure, where #2469's prompt-drift detector has never emitted a sample in any environment and its silence has read as health ever since. This series is written on EVERY sweep tick, so the healthy state is an explicit 0 you can see. A NON-ZERO value is not yet an error: a claude-code-cloud run suspended on subscription usage limits legitimately sits here for hours and answers later, possibly the next morning (#2473). What matters is a value that STAYS up as it approaches the TTL. Always read this panel together with the heartbeat beside it — a zero here means "nobody is waiting" only if the sweep that wrote it is still running.

panels.title: Watchdog heartbeat (10m) — 0 means nothing is LOOKING (#2477)
panels.description: min(increase(agent_dispatch_sweeps_total{env="$env",channel="support"}[10m])) — #2477, the liveness anchor for the panel beside it, and the reason that panel's zero can be believed at all. DispatchTracker.sweep ticks every DispatchTracker.SweepInterval (60s) and counts itself on every tick, healthy ones included, so a healthy 10-minute window reads ~10. min() and not sum(), matching alert W12 exactly: the two are identical at numInstances: 1, but under a scale-out a sum would let one live instance's ticks hide a dead sweep fiber on its sibling — and this panel is where W12 sends you to check, so it must read the same quantity the alert does rather than a reassuring one. It is REQUIRED rather than nice-to-have because unreplied is a GAUGE: a gauge keeps exporting its last written value for as long as the process lives, so a sweep fiber that died would publish a stale, reassuring 0 indefinitely and the watchdog would go dark in exactly the way #2546 describes. ZERO HERE MEANS NOTHING IS LOOKING, and the unreplied panel must not be read at all. Rule out the two benign causes first: the support responder is flag-off in this environment (the sweep is forked only when support.responderEnabled is true — Main.scala), or the API restarted within the window. Anything else is a dead fiber — redeploy, and grep the API log for a sweep-loop failure. Alert W12 fires on this.

panels.title: Duplicate answers suppressed (#2668)
panels.description: sum by (op) (rate(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",outcome="superseded"}[5m])) — customer-visible agent callbacks (op ∈ reply | consent_request) DROPPED because a LATER dispatch owns that thread's turn. Every sample is a duplicate answer the customer did NOT receive. The prod shape (2026-08-09, #2668): a consent grant fired the #2460 resume, the customer went back to the chat and asked again exactly as the consent page tells them to, that dispatched a second session, and BOTH replied — two bot messages seconds apart saying the same thing in different words. Small and non-zero is HEALTHY: it counts follow-ups that raced a session already in flight, which is ordinary conversation. A sustained spike is not — dispatches are overlapping far more than the conversations warrant; read it against support_dispatch_total{outcome="dispatched"} and the callback-actions panel. A flat zero while overlapping dispatches are visible means the guard is not running: it is in-memory and per-process (DispatchTracker), and fails OPEN across a restart by design, since an answer nobody receives is worse than one received twice.
